faqs.a: Roman numerals are the ancient Roman number system: I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000. They are still used on clocks, book chapters and movie sequels.
Subtractive pairs avoid repeating a symbol four times: 4 is IV (not IIII) and 900 is CM (not DCCCC). Smaller-before-larger means subtract.
The standard form tops out at 3999 (MMMCMXCIX) because there is no standard symbol above M=1000 in common use. Larger numbers used overlines, which keyboards cannot type.
faqs.q: Why does the converter stop at 3999?

faqs.a: Only in the standard form. Ancient Romans and modern clock faces sometimes used IIII for 4 — the converter accepts only the standard IV.
No. Roman numerals have no symbol for zero and no negative numbers — they were designed for counting physical things.

roman-numeral-converter.quickAnswer: Roman numerals use seven letters: I(1), V(5), X(10), L(50), C(100), D(500), M(1000). To convert, take the largest symbol that fits and repeat — 2024 becomes MMXXIV. A smaller symbol before a larger one subtracts, so IV is 4 and CM is 900.
roman-numeral-converter.tagline: Convert between numbers and Roman numerals.
roman-numeral-converter.workedExample:
Convert 2024 to Roman numerals.

2000 = MM (2 × 1000).
20 = XX (2 × 10).
4 = IV.

2024 = MM + XX + IV = MMXXIV.

Reading back: MMXXIV = 1000 + 1000 + 10 + 10 + 4 = 2024. Correct.
